memory_candidates.content: When building a stub PATH directory to mask one specific binary (e.g. sha256sum) for a shell-script test, resolve each kept binary with `type -P`, not `command -v`. In a Claude Code harness session, `command -v` can resolve a name to an exported shell FUNCTION (e.g. a wrapped `grep`) rather than a real path, even inside a freshly-invoked non-interactive `bash script.sh` subprocess, because bash functions exported via BASH_FUNC_*%% env vars propagate to children. `type -P` looks only in PATH for a real executable, bypassing functions/aliases/builtins, and is the correct primitive for this idiom.

This repo's task-ref-ok exemption marker (strip_exempt_regions in task-reference-patterns.sh) is a flat awk state machine with no nesting counter: a line matching task-ref-ok:begin sets in_block=1, and the NEXT line matching task-ref-ok:end sets in_block=0 unconditionally, regardless of any outer wrapper already active. If a file already has one outer begin/end pair spanning its whole body, inserting a SECOND, nested begin/end pair around a sub-range closes the OUTER block early at the nested :end, silently un-exempting everything after it. The repo-wide check-task-references.sh lint (which scans the full file) catches this, but the write-time PreToolUse hook (validate-no-task-references.sh) does not, because it only scans the Edit's own new_string in isolation. Fix: add a lone, no-op task-ref-ok:begin inside the new_string (satisfies the hook) and never add a matching :end when an outer wrapper already covers the region.
